dialogue.text: I am, for a little while longer, a PhD Candidate at UC Berkeley in the Berkeley Institute of Design Lab. In September I'm starting as a postdoctoral fellow with The Smithsonian!

_note: hand puppets 3 Adobe Research, 4 Midjourney Storytelling Lab, 5 tiat — cycle for each 'here'

dialogue.text: You may know me for being a critical HCI + AI + Design researcher and creative technologist---I've been publishing papers and performing stunts at places like here, here, and here!

_note: hand puppet 6: bPigment

dialogue.text: my research has gone from designing novel color mixing and digital painting systems…

_note: hand puppet 7: CSE

dialogue.text: to empirically studying creative communities, and the sociotechnical ecosystems that support them — including the supportive and disruptive roles that technology can play in those ecosystems —

_note: full-screen artographer video

dialogue.text: …to my current focus on cultural and historical data work, designing interactions that lead us towards engaging with, appreciating, and sustaining human artists and art-making.

_note: hand puppets 8, 9, 10: photos/videos of teaching + student work — cycle

dialogue.text: I've also had the privilege of teaching Creative Programming and Electronics at Berkeley for the past 3 years, together with the great Dr. Sudhu Tewari, and getting to take credit for our students' amazing work.

_note: hand puppets 11–15: shm's art (5) — cycle

dialogue.text: …but the role and identity I've laid claim to, and have held most dear, for the longest time, is being...an artist!

_note: hand puppets 16–20: shm's college art (5) — cycle

dialogue.text: Before my PhD, I studied computer science & fine art at The College of New Jersey, with a focus on self-portraiture, oil painting and charcoal.

dialogue.text: and before that, I was...… and I know this revelation may be shocking to some…

dialogue.text: these days, I've been interested in combining my love of performance… visual art… and creative computation.

dialogue.text: I'm curious what each of these mediums & practices can learn and take and shift in each other, and I think the best and most fun way to investigate this has been through creative practice and making and performing.

_note: full-screen video of shm performing painting

dialogue.text: I've been experimenting with performing self-portraiture, the act of painting my self, alongside a computational system that is also trying to 'paint' me. I'll be performing this piece next week at Central St. Martens in London!

_note: left stage puppet: sock puppet, bouncing + mouth-animated (enable mic in the panel first!)

dialogue.text: as you can maybe see. I've been experimenting with digital puppetry.

_note: sock stage puppet persists

dialogue.text: compared to my other work, I really like how this use of 'AI' has given me the opportunity to express and practice, develop, and embody some of my opinions about it. Namely,

_note: nothing on screen

dialogue.text: that I don't want our society to train some fancy big model capable of artificial general intelligence.

_note: three stage puppets L/M/R: sock, sock+hat, sock+puppeteer — each bounces + animates

dialogue.text: I want us to make a bunch of scrappy little models capable of real specific stupidity.

_note: potato tracking ON (box + 'potato' label), everything else off

dialogue.text: for example, yesterday I took a small, general-purpose potato detection dataset. which already is pretty stupid. and I trained it to bias it towards recognizing this specific potato.
and it brought me to reflect on how. I'm very tired of technology designed to be 'general purpose', and I'll give you two reasons why.
one, anything that presents itself as 'general' inherently perpetuates, and helps codify, some way of framing the world that says

_note: drawing mode ON (white) — shm draws the normal distribution

dialogue.text: those at the center of some general, normal distribution are a priority, and anyone in the margins is an unfortunate edge case

_note: clear the drawing, drawing mode off

dialogue.text: and two, because anything designed to perform generally tends to perform.... generically.  which is boring.
I am not often moved by genericism.

every piece of media, and every person and animal and plant and bug that I have loved, I loved because it is distinct and impossibly specific and therefore an absolute miracle to share even a moment with, as I too am but a finite blip within an infinite void of space and time and—

_note: potato capture, normal bounding box

dialogue.text: —um…. back to why I trained this model to recognize this specific potato.
it's because I really wanted to be able to do this, specifically.

_note: Mr. Potato Head accessories appear on the potato. Manual fallback ('p') armed.

dialogue.text: …and this, of course.

_note: Mrs. Potato Head accessories on the potato
hand puppet 24: legacy BART costume

dialogue.text: something I love about doing performance art in collaboration with technology, including stuff like costume making….
this is my BART costume.

_note: hand puppet 25: 2nd / new BART costume

dialogue.text: …and this is my 2nd BART costume.
is that it creates these stakes, where you have to solve problems you never even imagined being a problem. for example, last night, I was doing this in my kitchen.

_note: full-screen video of shm doing the potato training

dialogue.text: …to collect a training dataset. of this specific potato.
and in a world shaped by the desperate clawing of technosolutionism, and a subsequent overabundance of technology solutions,
and this inordinate pressure on computer scientists and technology designers, like myself and my peers and students, to always be inventing bigger and smarter technology solutions...

_note: potato overlay: a silly cat

dialogue.text: it's kind of artistically cathartic to invent low-stakes problems, for a particularly stupid and useless potato AI to solve.

_note: face mesh on

dialogue.text: as an edge-case kind of person, it's also been so cathartic and interesting to use this medium to confront and explore these questions of recognition. of masking.

_note: surveillance-critique models on: race/gender/age/emotion + bbox

dialogue.text: of what it means to be recognized by a system. to make yourself recognizable, legible.

_note: stage direction: smile to continue

dialogue.text: what it means to live in a world where the thing you are recognized as is not authentic to who you are, or how you feel on the inside.

gee thanks max. anyway, I think the narrative and rhetorical possibilities here are super intriguing. what does it mean to be recognized, and labeled?

dialogue.text: ok, thank you max. and thanks everyone for your time and attention, and to our community leaders and organizers for allowing me to be a part of this beautiful program and community.

I'm really excited to create art, and experiences, together, with all of you, this summer at stochastic — in this really distinct moment of time and space that I, miraculously, get to share together with each of you.
